```{r setup}
library(vgplotr)
```

Every plot vgplotr renders is ultimately answered by a live SQL query
against a DuckDB database -- that's what makes mosaic's plots interactive
and scalable in the first place. By default that database is DuckDB-Wasm,
a real DuckDB compiled to WebAssembly and run entirely inside the browser
(see `vignette("getting-started")` for the basics: `vg_data()`, `file =`,
`query =`, and `sql()`/`agg()` for raw SQL expressions, all of which work
the same way regardless of which database is actually running underneath).
This article is about the *other* option: rendering against a real, native
DuckDB process instead.

## Why you'd want native DuckDB instead of DuckDB-Wasm

DuckDB-Wasm keeps a rendered plot fully self-contained and shareable as
plain HTML, which is why it's vgplotr's default. But it's still DuckDB
running inside a browser sandbox, which caps how much data it can
comfortably hold and how far it can reach: it can't run DuckDB's own
federation extensions -- `postgres_scanner`/`ATTACH ... (TYPE postgres)`,
`mysql_scanner`, `sqlite_scanner` -- that let a *native* DuckDB process
transparently query Postgres, MySQL, or SQLite as if they were ordinary
local tables. If your data is too large for the browser, or actually
lives in one of those other databases, native DuckDB is the way to reach
it.

## `vg_duckdb_connector()`

`vg_widget()`/`vg_render()` accept a `connector =` argument: the default
is `vg_wasm_connector()` (DuckDB-Wasm, as above); `vg_duckdb_connector()`
switches to a real DuckDB process instead, started on your own machine and
reached over a small local server that vgplotr manages for you.

```r
# vgplotr creates and manages its own private native DuckDB connection
big_data |> vg_mark_dot(x = ~a, y = ~b) |> vg_render(connector = vg_duckdb_connector())
```

Everything else about building a spec -- `vg_data()`, `vg_mark_*()`,
`vg_interactor()`, transforms, `sql()`/`agg()` -- works exactly the same
way; only how the resulting SQL actually gets executed changes.

## Reaching an external database

Since DuckDB's federation extensions are just ordinary SQL, vgplotr
doesn't need any special code to support them -- set up a connection
however you'd normally use DuckDB from R, and hand it to
`vg_duckdb_connector()`:

```r
con <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb())
DBI::dbExecute(con, "INSTALL postgres; LOAD postgres; ATTACH 'dbname=mydb host=...' AS pg (TYPE postgres)")

vg_create() |>
  vg_data(name = "orders", query = "SELECT * FROM pg.orders") |>
  vg_mark_dot(data_from = "orders", x = ~date, y = ~amount) |>
  vg_render(connector = vg_duckdb_connector(con))
```

`vg_data(query = ...)` is the same option used for any SQL-defined data
source (see `vignette("getting-started")`) -- here it just happens to
query a table that DuckDB is transparently proxying to Postgres. A `con`
you supply yourself is never closed by vgplotr; you own its lifecycle.

Only one native connection is served per R session -- if you need to
switch to a different `con`, call `vg_duckdb_server_stop()` first.

## What you need installed

Native DuckDB rendering needs the `duckdb` and `nanoarrow` packages
(`install.packages(c("duckdb", "nanoarrow"))`); neither is required for
the default DuckDB-Wasm path, so plain `vg_widget(spec)` never needs them.

## Sharing and security

This article's examples aren't demonstrated live, because native-DuckDB
output behaves differently from DuckDB-Wasm output in one important way:
**it's only interactive on the machine/session that rendered it.** The
browser talks to a small local server started for that R session; opening
the rendered page again later, or on another machine, gives a plot that
can't connect to anything. DuckDB-Wasm output has no such limitation --
it's genuinely self-contained -- which is exactly why it stays vgplotr's
default.

The local server also has no authentication: it runs whatever SQL the
page sends it (mosaic's own generated queries, in normal use), mitigated
by binding to `127.0.0.1` only, never a public network interface. Don't
point `vg_duckdb_connector()` at a connection with more access than you'd
want a browser tab to have -- prefer a read-only role or connection when
attaching to a real external database. See `?vg_duckdb_connector` and
`?vg_duckdb_server_stop` for the full details.
